en: And then there also is support for
transactions. So again, if you have multiple
statements that should be executed together,
and if one of them fails, all should be
rolled back,
that can be done with a transaction, and
Bun's SQL client supports it. You start a
transaction by calling begin on it. So
instead of creating a tagged template
literal like we did before, we instead call
a method on SQL, the begin method.
That method takes an async callback
function, and in that callback function, you
use the transaction
parameter, which you get automatically
provided by Bun. You use that to create a
tagged template literal instead of SQL
inside of that callback, which you pass to
begin.
And that then is your SQL statement, your
command, your query you wanna execute as
part of a
transaction. And of course, here you could
have multiple
queries, right? And they would all be
executed in one transaction. And again, if
one of them fails, all of them fail and are
rolled back. That's the idea.
And just as before, you have to await each
statement in there to actually then execute
it, and you have to await the overall
transaction to actually execute it. And that
is all. That's how transactions are set up
and executed. And Bun's SQL client supports
them out of the way. And just as the SQLite
client, the SQL client also has a close
method to close the database.
